name: Hearthvale
summary: The vale where the Nine Hearths lit their nine fires during the War of Heaven's Edge, and where the Compact was dissolved a thousand years later. Not ruined — retired. The terraces stand, the hearth-platforms remain, and the last fire has been kept alive ever since by whoever passes: a custom older than every kingdom on Aurelith.
original_role: capital of the Nine Hearths (see factions/extinct-orders.json)

current_state.access: open to all who come on foot; the folk-custom of hearth-right holds here absolutely
current_state.condition: overgrown terraces, nine stone hearth-platforms in a ring, one fire kept burning by travelers for ~3,400 years
current_state.inhabitants: none permanent. A rotation of the devout, the homeless, and the hunted keeps the Last Fire. Verdant kin prune the vale's trees but never settle.

sites.name: The Nine Hearths
sites.description: Nine stone platforms in a ring, each scorched black from a century of use. Eight are cold. The ninth — the Stranger's Hearth, open to any who flee — holds the Last Fire.

sites.name: The Last Fire
sites.description: Burning continuously since before the Concord. Fed by every traveler who passes; it has never once gone out. Local law in three realms treats extinguishing it as the oldest crime there is.

sites.name: The Moot Stones
sites.description: Nine seats of raised earth where the hearth-moots were held. Speech made here is traditionally safe — even the Censer honors this, though no treaty requires it.

sites.name: The Shared Graves
sites.description: Where the Nine Hearths buried the dead of both divine armies. Ground no god may claim, by the Compact's first vow. Greenfolk tend it; deep-folk cut its markers; neither claims it.

hazards: None by intent — which makes the vale the safest place on Aurelith, and the most watched
Censer observers record visitors' names at the vale's edge; the Moonwardens record the same list and falsify it
adventure_hooks: A fugitive Glimmerborn begs escort to the Last Fire: within the vale, even the Censer's writ pauses — officially
The Last Fire guttered for the first time in living memory last Duskfall; the devout want investigators, the Censer wants them followed
Beneath the moot stones, someone has begun digging. The graves must not be opened — every faith on Aurelith agrees, which means someone will try
